governance.rule: Do not attribute the full repair/restoration account to the ballroom without project-level accounting.

primary_sources.title: Budget of the U.S. Government FY 2027 — Executive Office of the President appendix
supported_findings: The White House Repair and Restoration account received a very large 2026 federal-source funding stream compared with its ordinary direct appropriation.
The 2026 budget table records $350 million in mandatory spending authority from offsetting collections and $377 million in reimbursable obligations.
The official table independently supports the existence of substantial taxpayer-backed activity in the White House repair/restoration account.
limitations: The table does not identify the originating federal agency for each dollar.
The table does not by itself allocate the full $350 million or $377 million to the ballroom/East Wing project.
Project-level transfer, obligation, invoice, and contract records remain required.

primary_sources.title: Application for Stay, National Park Service v. National Trust for Historic Preservation, No. 26A203
supported_findings: The government characterizes the East Wing project as a highly integrated military complex incorporating a secured ballroom and national-security facilities.
The filing describes five below-ground stories and multiple military/security features.
The filing simultaneously states that approximately $400 million in private donations funds the ballroom and that zero taxpayer dollars are needed or required for the ballroom.
primary_sources.analytical_significance: The government's own filing makes the scope boundary explicit: one integrated physical project, while its funding claim is phrased specifically around the ballroom component. That makes project/component accounting essential.
limitations: The filing is advocacy by a litigating party and does not independently audit project finances.

primary_sources.title: The White House Announces White House Ballroom Construction to Begin
supported_findings: The original announcement described an approximately $200 million structure funded by President Trump and other donors.
The same announcement separately assigned necessary security enhancements and modifications to the United States Secret Service.
limitations: This is a public funding assertion, not audited expenditure evidence.
It does not quantify Secret Service costs.
